provenance.task: Quantify corpus sensitivity (the size of a real, non-noise difference between two measurements of the same shipped config) on the live corpus, per team-lead request after model_ab/chunking_ab runs minutes apart disagreed in direction (p6-boostfix). RENAMED from 'noise floor' on 2026-07-28 per team-lead + p6-mechanism: p6-mechanism ran 152 same-config re-measurements across 11 corpus states and found 60 independent full rebuilds at an UNCHANGED corpus (chunk_count 6,644, two separate index directories, non-consecutive) bit-identical on every metric -- zero variance. This pipeline has no measurement noise. Every spread recorded in this file (including all values below, unchanged by this rename) is corpus sensitivity: the corpus genuinely differed between the compared runs. See corpus_determinism_proof below.
provenance.label: corpus sensitivity: 3x replicate re-runs of both A/Bs, boost=0.0, code held fixed (formerly labelled 'noise floor' -- see task field above for why that name was wrong)
provenance.method: Ran model_ab.run_model_ab() and chunking_ab.run_chunking_ab() 3 times each, back to back, same commit, same boost, no code changes between runs -- the only thing that can vary is the live ~/.claude/projects corpus, which other agents in this session are still writing to. The spread (max-min) of each (config, metric) pair across the 3 replicates is corpus sensitivity, not measurement noise: p6-mechanism's 60 bit-identical rebuilds at a fixed corpus (see corpus_determinism_proof below) prove this pipeline has none. Where the spread is nonzero, the corpus changed between replicates; where it's exactly 0.0, the corpus happened not to change in that window -- not because short windows are inherently more precise.

corpus_determinism_proof.source: First-hand: p6-mechanism ran this study and wrote it up directly (rpt-p6-mechanism.md, this session's scratchpad). Team-lead relayed the finished report to p6-boostfix for filing here -- ordinary task routing, not a second act of research or an intermediate witness in a chain of hearsay. p6-boostfix independently re-verified the load-bearing numbers below directly against p6-mechanism's raw data before committing this block (see `verification` field) -- corrected 2026-07-28 after p6-mechanism flagged that the original wording here read like second-hand reporting and caused this first-hand result to be treated as such.
corpus_determinism_proof.finding: 152 same-config re-measurements across 11 corpus states. 60 independent full rebuilds at an unchanged corpus (chunk_count 6,644), run non-consecutively across two separate index directories, produced bit-identical results on every metric -- overall and all five per-class MRR and recall values. Zero variance. MAIN_SESSION_BOOST verified 0.0 computationally on all 152 measurements.
corpus_determinism_proof.conclusion: Indexing, embedding, BM25, and ranking are all deterministic in this pipeline. No amount of re-running the eval at a fixed corpus state would ever produce a different number. The only source of any spread recorded anywhere in this file is the corpus genuinely differing between the two (or three) compared measurements.
corpus_determinism_proof.practical_implication: Averaging repeated eval runs to 'tighten' a number is not useful here -- at a fixed corpus, N runs give one value to the last bit, not N noisy samples of a true mean. The only way to reduce the spread recorded below is to pin the corpus state (e.g. compare two runs against the identical index, or accept that any two measurements taken at different real-world times may legitimately differ by up to the amounts recorded in `floors` below).
corpus_determinism_proof.method: Invoked eval/harness.py through its own CLI (`.venv/bin/python eval/harness.py --index-dir <private dir> --json-out <path>`, no --main-session-boost flag), 152 times. main_session_boost verified computationally on EVERY run, not sampled -- both stdout ('main_session_boost = 0.0') and the JSON payload's own field checked; all 152 read 0.0. 11 distinct chunk_count corpus states observed (6,637-6,647; episode_count 3,750-3,760), spanning ~14.5 minutes of wall-clock time on the live, concurrently-written corpus. 152 runs distributed across those 11 states, 2-60 replicates per state. The bit-identity determinism proof specifically rests on the 60 replicates at chunk_count=6,644 -- per p6-mechanism, run non-consecutively across two independently-created private index directories (two separate background batches), not one build re-read 60 times.
corpus_determinism_proof.verification: p6-boostfix independently re-derived the load-bearing numbers directly from p6-mechanism's raw data (not just their prose) before writing this block: loaded both p6mech_samples.jsonl (45 rows) and p6mech_samples_b2.jsonl (107 rows) = 152 total; confirmed exactly 11 distinct chunk_count values (6637-6647); confirmed exactly 60 rows at chunk_count=6644; confirmed all 152 rows' main_session_boost field reads 0.0; confirmed all 60 chunk_count=6644 rows' `summary` JSON content is byte-identical (1 distinct value in the set of 60). Did NOT independently re-verify the 'two separate index directories' infrastructure detail beyond what p6-mechanism's own report states (rpt-p6-mechanism.md's Method section) -- the flat sample JSONL has no field distinguishing which physical index_dir produced a given row, so that specific detail is relayed from the authoritative source, not independently confirmed; the substantive claim (60 bit-identical results at one unchanged corpus state) IS independently confirmed. Raw data and 152 individual --json-out files: p6mech_samples.jsonl / p6mech_samples_b2.jsonl and p6mech_runs/ / p6mech_runs_b2/, this session's scratchpad. Full report: rpt-p6-mechanism.md (same directory) -- also covers a corpus-size-vs-MRR mechanism study (rpt-p6-mechanism.md itself) and a follow-up gap-variability study (rpt-p6-mechanism-gap.md, see matched_pair_gap_study_2026-07-28.json for that one's committed form).

floors.note: Two distinct floors, not one -- collapsing them into a single number understates MRR's sensitivity and overstates recall's. Both are CORPUS-SENSITIVITY floors, not measurement-noise floors: p6-mechanism's 60 bit-identical rebuilds at an unchanged corpus (see provenance.corpus_determinism_proof) prove this pipeline has zero inherent noise, so every number below reflects how much a real corpus difference can move a metric, not measurement imprecision. 'instantaneous_tight_loop' is measured directly from the 3x replicate spreads in model_ab_replicates/chunking_ab_replicates above (runs seconds apart, same script invocation) -- every value below is read programmatically from that data, not retyped. It reads ~0 in most cases NOT because short time windows are inherently precise, but because the corpus usually didn't change in that window (confirmed by direct index inspection in determinism_investigation below, where it did). 'cross_experiment_minutes_apart' compares this session's replicate group (index builds at 20:36:39-20:37:09) against abrerun's independently-committed run (~20:28) -- same code, same config, ~8-9 minutes apart, so the only variable able to differ is the live corpus, and it measurably did.

recall_at_10.instantaneous_tight_loop_note: 0.0 for chunking_ab's uniform/per_turn (13s replicate span; the corpus did not change in that window -- see determinism_investigation below for the direct evidence, not an inference from the short elapsed time); 0.0278 (one query at n=36) for model_ab's potion-retrieval-32M, whose replicate window DID catch a real corpus change. Recall is a step function -- it only moves when a query's rank crosses the top-10 boundary, so it reads exactly 0 unless the corpus changed AND that change happened to touch one of the 36 labelled queries.
recall_at_10.recommended_bound_note: Per-class deltas (n=9 per class in this label set) must be read against 1/9 = 0.1111, not the overall-level 0.0278 -- a class recall swing of one query out of 9 is exactly this floor, not a finding on its own.

mrr.instantaneous_tight_loop_note: 0.0 (bit-identical across all 3 replicates) for both of chunking_ab's arms -- corpus unchanged during that replicate window, not 'instantaneously precise' as a property of short elapsed time (compare model_ab's potion-retrieval-32M in the same table, whose window DID catch a corpus change and shows real spread). 0.0060 for model_ab's potion-base-8M, the largest instantaneous MRR spread seen anywhere in this data.
mrr.cross_experiment_measurement: abrerun's committed chunking_ab.json uniform-arm overall MRR (0.5582, 4-decimal precision -- this is the only precision ever captured for that value; the source file was overwritten by this session's own regeneration before higher precision was recorded, and was never git-committed, so it cannot be recovered to more decimals) vs this session's replicate group's uniform-arm overall MRR (0.5465939153439153, full precision, bit-identical across all 3 runs) -- same code, same config, ~9 minutes apart, only the corpus differs -- this delta IS corpus sensitivity, measured directly, not an estimate of measurement error. Delta reported to 4 decimals to match the less-precise input, not fabricated further.
mrr.recommended_bound_note: Use ~0.012 as the practical corpus-sensitivity bound for comparisons between runs separated by minutes or more (i.e. essentially all cross-experiment or cross-report comparisons in this repo) -- see cross_experiment_30min_observed below for evidence this may still understate longer windows. Use the much smaller instantaneous range (0.0-0.0060) only when comparing runs from the same tight back-to-back loop AND the corpus is confirmed (not assumed) unchanged between them.
mrr.outlier_investigation_update: team-lead + p6-docfix identified the original baseline_boost_0.0 artifact (built ~20:22) as an outlier vs. 8 other same-config measurements built 20:36-20:52 -- 0.055-0.070 above the cluster on exact-identifier MRR, 5-6x this floor. Discriminating test: regenerated the baseline via eval/harness.py (same builder) on the current, later corpus. Result: landed in the cluster (~0.86 exact-identifier, ~0.54 overall), not near the old outlier (0.926 / 0.558) -- CONFIRMS corpus growth over time, not a builder difference between eval/harness.py and model_ab.py/chunking_ab.py. eval/results/baseline_boost_0.0_2026-07-27.json has been replaced with this regeneration; see its own provenance.
mrr.cross_experiment_30min_measurement: Original baseline_boost_0.0 (now superseded, ~20:22, overall MRR 0.5582) vs. model_ab_2026-07-27.json's potion-base-8M arm (~20:52, overall MRR 0.5420) -- same shipped config, ~30 minutes apart, only the corpus differs. Real, measured corpus-growth drift (hypothesis 1 confirmed above) -- confirmed further by p6-mechanism's proof that this pipeline has zero inherent noise (provenance.corpus_determinism_proof), so there is no other candidate explanation for this delta besides the corpus itself differing.
mrr.recommended_bound_UPDATED: The 9-minute cross-experiment figure (0.0116, recommended_bound 0.012 above) understates drift over longer windows: 0.0162 was observed over ~30 minutes on this same live corpus. This bound scales with elapsed time between the two measurements being compared, because it is corpus sensitivity, not measurement noise -- more elapsed time means more opportunity for the corpus to have genuinely changed, not a wider error bar around a fixed true value. For a doc citing a single number with no fixed re-measurement cadence (i.e. the gap could be arbitrarily large), ~0.012 is now understood to be an underestimate; a more conservative figure in the 0.016-0.02 range is better supported by the data actually collected today. Not changed in tests/test_published_numbers.py's MRR_CROSS_EXPERIMENT_FLOOR constant per explicit team-lead instruction not to widen the guard's tolerance -- this field is guidance for whoever next revisits that constant or the four documents citing ±0.012, not a silent self-update.

determinism_investigation.question: team-lead: model_ab's replicates were not fully deterministic (e.g. potion-retrieval-32M error-string recall moved 0.889->1.0, subagent-only 0.692->0.769) while chunking_ab's were bit-identical across all 3. Is this corpus growth during the longer model_ab runs, or something non-deterministic in the 512-dimension path?
determinism_investigation.answer: Not fully established -- corpus growth is a confirmed contributing factor, but does not by itself explain the asymmetry (see revised evidence below). Per team-lead direction: not investigated further, since potion-retrieval-32M is a deferred, unshipped candidate, not a code path anything currently running exercises. Caveat recorded below for whoever revisits the model swap.
evidence: Inspected all 6 model_ab replicate index builds directly (episode counts + file mtimes, via sqlite3 against the actual built index.db files, not summaries): episode_count held at 3496 for the first 3 builds (potion-base-8M runs 0-1 and potion-retrieval-32M run 0, timestamps 20:36:39-20:36:45), then rose to 3497 for the remaining 3 builds (20:36:47-20:36:53). Exactly one episode landed mid-sequence.

The immediately-following chunking_ab replicate sequence (6 index builds, 20:36:56-20:37:09) held episode_count=3497 for all 6 builds -- zero growth in that entire window. This, not a difference in determinism between the two scripts, is why chunking_ab's replicates came out bit-identical and model_ab's did not: chunking_ab's window simply didn't catch a write.

The growth event has no relationship to embedding dimension: model_ab replicate run 1's potion-base-8M build (20:36:45, ep=3496) preceded the growth; that SAME replicate's potion-retrieval-32M build 2 seconds later (20:36:47, ep=3497) landed just after it. Growth is a function of wall-clock time elapsed since script start, not of which model or dimension is being encoded.

Per-build timing is comparable between the two scripts (~2-3s between a model_ab replicate's two model builds; ~2s between a chunking_ab replicate's two chunking-strategy builds) -- model_ab is not meaningfully slower per build in this data. The difference in observed determinism came down to which ~15-second window happened to catch a concurrent agent's session write in this live, shared corpus, not a property of either script or the 512-dim encoding path.

Team-lead catch, and the reason 'corpus growth' alone is not treated as the full explanation above: potion-base-8M's own 3 replicate builds straddle the SAME growth event (2 builds at episode_count=3496, 1 at 3497 -- the growth landed between its run-1 and run-2 builds) yet potion-base-8M showed ZERO recall@10 spread and only a small MRR spread (0.0060), while potion-retrieval-32M straddled the same event (1 build at 3496, 2 at 3497) and showed the full 0.0278 recall spread. Growth alone does not obviously explain why one config was insensitive to the new episode and the other was not -- a plausible, mundane explanation is that the two models score the new episode's content differently against these 36 queries (a borderline-relevant chunk can cross a top-10 threshold under one embedding and not another) rather than genuine non-determinism in encoding the same text twice, but this is not verified and is exactly the kind of thing 'cause not established' below is honest about.
determinism_investigation.caveat_for_future_readers: The 512-dimension path (potion-retrieval-32M) was the least reproducible configuration tested; cause not established.
determinism_investigation.update_2026_07_28: p6-mechanism's 60-rebuild bit-identity proof (provenance.corpus_determinism_proof) directly bears on the open 'cause not established' caveat below: it proves indexing/embedding/BM25/ranking are fully deterministic at a fixed corpus, which rules out genuine non-determinism in the 512-dimension encoding path as an explanation for potion-retrieval-32M's greater sensitivity to the mid-sequence corpus change. The straddle-asymmetry evidence below therefore reduces to: the two models are differently SENSITIVE to the same corpus change (a mundane, expected property -- different embeddings have different decision boundaries), not that one model's pipeline is less reproducible than the other's. Still not investigated further, per the original team-lead instruction (potion-retrieval-32M remains deferred and unshipped) -- recorded here because leaving this section's 'cause not established' language sitting uncontradicted next to new evidence that actually narrows it down would itself be exactly the kind of stale claim this whole file exists to avoid.

corpus_sensitivity.stale_value_notice: REVISED 2026-07-28 (team-lead gate 5): the ORIGINAL notice below this one (see superseded_stale_value_notice) justified using each config's single-arm instantaneous floor (~0.006) as the denominator for a 'multiple of floor' ratio, on the theory that two arms built in the same script run, seconds apart, are a matched pair that cancels corpus sensitivity. p6-mechanism directly tested this with a 36-run matched-pair study (eval/results/matched_pair_gap_study_2026-07-28.json) and falsified it: the GAP's own spread (0.0431 model / 0.0361 chunking) is LARGER than either arm's individual spread in both cases -- matched-pairing does not cancel corpus sensitivity here, it can amplify it (plausible mechanism: two different configs respond to the same new corpus content with weak or negative covariance, so Var(gap) = Var(A) + Var(B) - 2*Cov(A,B) can exceed max(Var(A), Var(B)) -- not independently confirmed, flagged as likely not fact). The overall_recall_at_10 / overall_mrr gap VALUES themselves are unaffected by this correction and remain exactly (retrieval-32M or per_turn's overall value) minus (base-8M or uniform's overall value), re-derivable from the co-committed model_ab_2026-07-27.json / chunking_ab_2026-07-27.json -- only the interpretive ratio/verdict fields next to them were wrong, now fixed against the correct (gap's own measured spread) denominator, sourced from a committed artifact rather than an assumption.
